segments.text: DoorDash is completely reinventing the food delivery space.
And I don't think people fully realize what they're actually working on under the hood.
Last week, they announced a ton of new features at their annual event.
Now, the biggest one to me was their ultra quiet food delivery drone DoorDash Air.
This thing can fly straight from a restaurant to your yard over top of all the traffic and dramatically reduces delivery times.
But it turns out this drone program is only a small piece of their overall master plan.
So to learn more, I sat down with Stanley Tang, one of the original co-founders and head of labs at DoorDash.
He is the mastermind behind the air launch and he runs their R&D lab.
And what he said really surprised me.
And a large part of what we built, we would call it the autonomous delivery platform.
Think of it as the orchestration layer, the brains behind the scenes that actually does all the coordination.
Is it a dasher?
Is it a drone?
Is it a dot?
That's what's magical about working with someone like DoorDash.
We handle all that complexity.
So the secret sauce at DoorDash isn't just the drones, it's the entire delivery operating system layer they've built to sit underneath.
Because DoorDash now has lots of different ways to deliver your food.
They've got dashers, the human drivers, DOT, the autonomous robot, and now AIR, the delivery drones.
So when an order comes in, they're able to intelligently route and deliver it in the fastest and most cost-efficient way possible.
And as they build more and more methods for delivery, including things like drones and autonomous vehicles, this will increase their ability to serve customers.
That orchestration layer underneath is the secret sauce behind why they're so effective.
Stanley also broke down how they're using AI in the new text DoorDash feature, as well as how he runs the R&D lab to drive new breakthroughs.
And it's clear they're doing everything they can to pioneer the future of delivery.
